newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Carmen Lawrence charged with perjury, steps aside.
newsitem.headline: Carmen Lawrence charged with perjury, steps aside.

text.p: Former Federal Health Minister Carmen Lawrence said three perjury charges served on her on Monday "are the end result of a highly politicised process".
"I am appalled that charges should be laid over a matter of differing recollections," Lawrence said in a statement in which she also declared her innocence.
Lawrence said she would stand down as the Federal Opposition's environment spokeswoman while the charges were before the courts.
However, she said she would not resign from Parliament where she is the member for Fremantle in the House of Representatives.

The perjury charges were served on Lawrence by Perth police who said they related to evidence given in 1995 to the Western Australian Royal Commission into the Use of Executive Power, also known as the Marks Royal Commission.
A police spokesman said John Halden, a Labor member of the Western Australian Legislative Council, had also been charged with one count of perjury in relation to the same matter.
"Both persons are summonsed to appear before the Perth Court of Petty Sessions in the Central Law Courts on Thursday, April 24," the spokesman said.
The Marks Royal Commission was set up to examine the circumstances surrounding the tabling of a controversial petition in the WA Parliament in 1992.
Four days after the petition was tabled a Perth lawyer, Mrs Penny Easton, who was named in the document, committed suicide.
In the Commission report tabled in State Parliament in late 1995, Kenneth Marks QC was critical of Lawrence's testimony regarding her knowledge of the petition before it was tabled.
